llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (turn conversation insights into full TED-style talks) is reasonable, but the runtime instructions are internally inconsistent about reading workspace/project artifacts and explicitly encourage using exact file names and metrics — this mismatch could lead to unnecessary disclosure of sensitive project data or confusion about what the agent will access.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill synthesizes conversation context into a long-form talk with examples and Q&A. Requesting concrete examples, narrative construction, and Q&A prep is coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md both (a) asserts the skill does NOT read files from the workspace or access project artifacts directly, and (b) repeatedly instructs the agent to 'collect concrete examples (files, metrics, decisions)' and to 'Include actual file names' and specific metrics. It also tells the agent to 'Read full conversation context.' These are inconsistent: either the skill will need the agent to access workspace/project files (which it says it won't) or it will prompt users to paste/supply sensitive details. The ambiguity could cause the agent to request or attempt to use sensitive file-level data without clear boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files (instruction-only). This minimizes disk writes and external install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested — requests for concrete examples are limited to conversational context or user-supplied content. That is proportionate, assuming the agent does not try to access files autonomously.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, the skill is user-invocable and does not request persistent privileges or system-wide configuration changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is primarily an instruction template and is plausible for converting discussion into a TED-style talk. However, SKILL.md is ambiguous about whether it will access project files: it explicitly says it does NOT read workspace files but also instructs including exact file names, metrics, and real decisions. Before installing or using it, confirm with the skill author whether the agent will ever read your repo or local files automatically. If you provide examples, sanitize or redact any sensitive filenames, secrets, or exact metrics you don't want exposed. Prefer pasting short, redacted excerpts into the conversation rather than granting any file-system access. If you need stronger assurance, ask the maintainer to clarify the data-handling behavior in the repository or add an explicit step that requires explicit user upload of any files the skill should use.
